ctor.rationale: `base(3, CardType.Attack, CardRarity.Ancient, TargetType.AnyEnemy)` (Whistle.cs:22-25) == cost 3 / ATTACK / ANCIENT / ANY_ENEMY.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new DamageVar(33m, ValueProp.Move)` (Whistle.cs:18) == `_damage = 33`, powered on both sides -- the largest single-hit damage number in the pool after card/bludgeon's 32 upgrades to 42.

OnPlay.issue: The damage is faithful and the STUN is the right verb. The divergence is the sim's extra `if not target.is_gone:` before it (whistle.py:86-87). C# calls `CreatureCmd.Stun(cardPlay.Target)` UNCONDITIONALLY (Whistle.cs:33), and `Stun` has NO liveness guard at all -- it is a bare `creature.StunInternal(Wrapper, nextMoveId)` plus a VFX wrapper (CreatureCmd.cs:870-903), with no `IsAlive`, `IsHittable` or `CombatState != null` test anywhere in either overload. So this is the card/bash family with a different verb: for an ordinary kill the two agree (`CreatureCmd.Damage` runs `Kill` before returning, CreatureCmd.cs:409, and removal at 523-525 detaches the creature), but for a corpse whose removal was VETOED (`Hook.ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath`, CreatureCmd.cs:508; the sim's `retained_after_death`, cmds.py:100-104) the game STUNS it and the sim does not -- and a retained corpse still takes turns, so being stunned actually skips one. LIVE: the retained-corpse path is ported (ReattachPower, powers.py:2360-2365; `combat.py:292,306`) and Whistle is a ported Ancient from Tanx's Whistle. Same family and same verdict as card/bash's OnPlay entry (rule 3), and the only member of it whose payload is a STUN rather than a power -- so the observable is the corpse's skipped turn rather than a Vicious draw. Presentation, folded in: WithHitFx and the StunIntent hover tip (16).
